slides.title: OOP Design and Lifecycle Management
content: Focuses on designing scalable and maintainable systems
Includes SOLID principles and object lifecycle
Helps manage memory and improve code quality

slides.title: SOLID Principles Overview
content: Five design principles for writing clean code
Includes SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP

slides.title: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
content: A class should have only one responsibility
One reason to change per class
Example: separate salary calculation and report generation

slides.title: Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
content: Classes should be open for extension but closed for modification
New functionality added without changing existing code
Example: adding new shapes without modifying existing classes

slides.title: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
content: Subclasses should replace parent classes without breaking behavior
Example: Penguin should not inherit flying behavior

slides.title: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
content: Classes should not implement unnecessary methods
Example: separate work() and eat() interfaces

slides.title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
content: Depend on abstractions, not concrete classes
Example: use Keyboard interface instead of WiredKeyboard class

slides.title: Object Lifecycle in Java
content: Object lifecycle defines stages of object existence

slides.title: Stages of Object Lifecycle
content: Creation: object created using new keyword
Usage: object methods and fields are used
Destruction: memory is freed by JVM

slides.title: Object Creation
content: Objects are created using new keyword

slides.title: System.gc()
content: Requests JVM to run garbage collection
JVM decides when to run GC

slides.title: Reference Concept
content: Objects become eligible for GC when no references exist
Reference variables point to heap objects
Null reference makes object eligible for GC

slides.title: Memory Leaks
content: Occurs when unused objects are not released

slides.title: Cyclic References
content: Objects reference each other forming a loop
Do not cause leaks in Java

slides.title: Summary
content: Object lifecycle ensures efficient memory usage
Together they ensure robust and scalable applications
